claim: FLYMV is the enter-and-move dragonfly routine this module ports.
FLYMV runs only while the player is alive — the PLAYP EOR 0A / PEXPLD gate at entry falls through only when both are clear.
The dragonfly spawn slot is motion object 12 (decimal) — BEEC+12 is probed for availability.
A non-zero BEEC+12 colour means the entry is taken and no dragonfly starts this tick.

source.verbatim: BNE 20$			;THIS IS NOT AN AVAILABLE ENTRY

claim: While the centipede is NOT dead (DEAD non-zero) the spawn goes through the mushroom-count check.
With the centipede dead, a beetle still on screen (BEETLS non-zero) skips the mushroom-count check entirely.

source.verbatim: BNE 18$			;IF BEETLE IS STILL ON THE SCREEN

claim: The mushroom threshold is BEEMV1 plus 30 hex, added with BEEMV1’s exit carry (set only on the 2F cap, making the ceiling 60 hex).
The threshold is compared against MUSH+2 — the near-the-top mushroom count; carry-clear (threshold below the count) blocks the spawn.

source.verbatim: BCC 20$			;TOO MANY MUSHROOMS AT THE TOP

claim: No dragonfly starts while CENTIN is 10 (decimal) or more — no flies if the centipede is nearly whole.
The movement scan runs slots 12 down to 0.
A picture code at or above 20 hex is not a dragonfly.
A picture code below 1E hex is not a dragonfly — the dragonfly band is exactly 1E..1F.
The wing flap toggles the picture with EOR 01.
In slow-down mode (SLOW non-zero) the wings flap every tick.
Outside slow-down mode the wings flap only on odd frames (FRAME AND 01 non-zero).
FLYMV1 exits with TEMP2+1 as the horizontal audio offset, -80 to +7F.
The horizontal wave starts from (FRAME AND 3F) shifted left twice.
Wave values in 40..BF are folded with EOR 7F, making a triangle wave.
BEEDH is an XOR mask applied to the wave — the wall-bounce direction state.
BEEH below 0E is the right edge.
BEEH at or above F4 is the left edge.
An edge bounce flips BEEDH with EOR FF.
An edge bounce also negates the current step (COMP of the pre-edge value).
The step is sign-extended and shifted left three times into a 16-bit value — eight times the wave byte.
In attract mode the score is treated as zero for the motion calculation.
From SCORE2 = 3 BCD (30,000) the step doubles again — sixteen times the wave byte.
The low byte accumulates into BEEHL and its carry rides into the BEEH add — fixed-point horizontal motion.
The dragonfly spawns with picture code 1E.
At SCORE2 = 15 BCD (150,000) and above the dragonfly is very fast — vertical speed 3.
At SCORE2 = 5 BCD (50,000) and above the dragonfly goes fast — vertical speed 2.
In bombing mode (NOCENT non-zero) the dragonfly is at least speed 2 even below 50,000.
Otherwise the dragonfly moves at vertical speed 1.
BEEMV2 sets the spawn V position to F8 (EOR CKF8 — identity upright).
The spawn H comes from RND0 masked with F8; a zero result is rejected and rerolled.
A masked value below 10 hex is off screen and rerolled too.
The accepted H is the masked value minus 4.
The spawn horizontal direction byte starts at zero.
The spawn colour byte is 79 — turning the object on.
BEEMV0 moves vertically by SUBTRACTING BEEDV from BEEV.
A post-move V below 4 is the bottom of the screen — the object leaves via BEEOFF.
BEEOFF zeroes PTS, then the colour and H bytes — the slot is freed.
The mushroom cell is taken 4 above the object (V+4, CKFF identity upright) — the mushroom appears after the object passes.

source.verbatim: LDA I,4			;MAKE MUSHROOM APPEAR AFTER BEE

claim: Attract mode always proceeds to the mushroom-planting logic.
In normal play, bombing mode (NOCENT non-zero) plants no mushrooms.
Mushrooms are planted only every fourth frame (FRAME AND 03 zero).

source.verbatim: BNE 28$			;PUT UP MUSHROOMS ONLY EVERY FOUR FRAMES

claim: A dragonfly above the player area (V at or above 48 hex) uses probability mask 01 — plant on half the random bytes.
Inside the player area the mask is 07 — fewer mushrooms, one byte in eight.

source.verbatim: LDA I,07		;LESS MUSHROOMS IN PLAYERS AREA

claim: The plant happens only when (mask AND RND1) is zero.
Below SCORE2 = 2 BCD (20,000) five mushrooms are needed.
From 20,000 up to 120,000 nine mushrooms are needed.
From SCORE2 = 12 BCD (120,000) the need is the halved SCORE2 byte plus 6.
The need caps at 2F — and the cap path exits with carry SET, which the FLYMV ADC folds in.
SHOOT2 dispatches picture codes 1E..1F (below 20, at or above 1E) to the dragonfly branch.
A shot dragonfly scores 500 points (Y = 5, BCD hundreds).
A dragonfly killed by DDT scores 1500 (Y = 15 BCD hundreds).
PTS is the 16-entry per-critter kill-points stamp array the title cites — BEEOFF clears this module’s entry.

source.verbatim: PTS:	.BLKB 16.		;NUMBER OF POINTS FOR KILLING THIS CRITTER

claim: MUSH is two counters — the second pair (MUSH+2) counts the mushrooms near the top, the one FLYMV reads.
SLOW is the timer that slows down all critters — the flap-every-tick mode.

source.verbatim: SLOW:	.BLKB 1			;TIMER FOR SLOWING DOWN ALL CRITTERS

claim: NOCENT non-zero is bombing mode — no centipedes are to be started.

source.verbatim: NOCENT:	.BLKB 1			;NON-ZERO IF NO CENTIPEDES ARE TO BE STARTED

claim: BEEHL is the motion-object fractional H byte the fixed-point step accumulates into.
MOSQT is the enter-and-move mosquito routine this module ports.
MOSQT runs only while the player is alive (the PLAYP/PEXPLD gate).
The mosquito spawn slot is motion object 12 (decimal) — BEEC+12.
Below SCORE2 = 7 BCD (70,000) the mosquito is less frequent — the full FRAME byte must match, one tick in 256.

source.verbatim: BCC 8$			;IF LESS THAN 70,000 MAKE MOSQUITO LESS FREQUENT

claim: At 70,000 and above FRAME is masked with 7F — a spawn tick every 128 frames, about 2 seconds.
The spawn tick fires when the (masked) frame equals 17 hex — the EOR 17 test, asynchronous with the rest of the program.

source.verbatim: 8$:	EOR I,17		;ASYNRONOUS WITH REST OF PROGRAM

claim: No mosquito starts while CENTIN is 9 or more.
A picture code at or above 10 hex is not a mosquito.
A picture code below 0E is not a mosquito — the band is exactly 0E..0F.
The wing flap toggles the picture with EOR 01.
In slow-down mode the wings flap every tick.
Otherwise the wings flap only on odd frames.
The mosquito moves horizontally by ADDING BEEDH to BEEH.
A post-move H below 0C is off the screen — bounce.
A post-move H below F5 is still on the screen; F5 and above bounces.
The bounce negates BEEDH via COMP — the overshot position itself is kept.
The mosquito moves vertically by SUBTRACTING BEEDV from BEEV.
A post-move V below 4 (EOR CKFF — identity upright) clears the object via BEEOFF.
After moving, MOSQT only runs the OBSTAC / DDTEXP / PLAY seams — there is no MUSHER call; the mosquito plants nothing.
The mosquito spawns with picture code 0E.
MOSQT3 initialises position and colour through the shared BEEMV2.
The default mosquito speed is 2.
At SCORE2 = 9 BCD (90,000) and above the mosquito is fast — speed 3.
RND1 bit 7 picks the horizontal direction — BEEDH is the speed or its COMP negation.
The negated direction is stored into BEEDH — the mosquito flies a random diagonal.
SHOOT2 dispatches picture codes below 10 hex (after the millipede band below 08) to the mosquito branch.
Killing a mosquito INCREMENTS SCROLC — the playfield scrolls UP one row.
A shot mosquito scores 400 points (Y = 4, BCD hundreds).
A mosquito killed by DDT scores 1200 (Y = 12 BCD hundreds).
SCROLC counts scrolls with sign — positive is up, negative is down.
BEEOFF zeroes PTS and frees the slot when the mosquito exits the bottom.
